comparator.name: Language and Culture Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: This example combines the Culture, Communication and Diversity core with an internship-based package. The internship counts within the specialization and fulfills the degree’s internship or study-abroad requirement.

components.name: Representations of Identity in Literature, Gender and Media
components.note: Introduces humanities research through historical and contemporary representations of identity.

components.name: Fact and Fiction in Communication and History
components.note: Examines framing and the reliability of sources.

components.name: Literary Analysis
components.note: One of the two introductory courses in the Dutch language area.

components.name: Introduction to Language and Communication
components.note: The Dutch language and communication course in the introductory pair.

components.name: Methods and Statistics 1
components.note: Develops empirical research design and basic statistical analysis.

components.name: Face-to-Face Communication
components.note: Prepares students for the core through the study of talk and interaction.

components.name: Intercultural Communication
components.note: Studies cultural differences in personal and public communication.

components.name: Cultural Representations
components.note: Studies how culture and diversity are represented.

components.name: Managing Linguistic Diversity
components.note: Studies how organizations and institutions respond to linguistic diversity.

components.name: Digital Identity
components.note: Studies identity and its expression in digital settings.

components.name: Knowledge for Society
components.note: Uses humanities research in collaboration with societal partners.

components.name: Audiovisual Media Practicum
components.note: Develops practical skills through a collaborative media project.

components.name: Internship
components.note: A 15 EC placement within the second package, subject to Utrecht approval.

components.name: Theory and Practice of the Humanities
components.note: Reflects on humanities methods, disciplinary knowledge and professional practice.

components.name: Communication Research Lab
components.note: Develops a research proposal before the thesis.

components.name: Communication and Information Studies Thesis
components.note: An independent supervised project connected to the core.

components.name: Electives
components.note: Open credit space subject to Utrecht’s degree rules.

notes.text: Utrecht students combine an approved specialization and a second package with electives. This example fulfills the internship or study-abroad requirement through an internship. The degree also requires a portfolio.
Utrecht requires a communication research lab and a thesis in this pathway. The UCR options develop research through courses and include a separate optional independent research element.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how language, art, media and history shape society. Utrecht teaches mainly in Dutch, with some courses in English. This example focuses on communication and cultural diversity.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Utrecht combines a communication core with practical humanities research and an internship. The UCR options focus on literature and art, film and digital culture, or colonial histories and gender.
